title: Daily Market Digest: October 8, 2026
subtitle: Clear, actionable market insights without specific investment advice.

items.headline: Indices Mixed Amid Hawkish Fed Stance and Surging Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. major indices showed a mixed performance today, as investor sentiment turned more defensive. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed higher, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite posted modest gains. This performance comes as rising oil prices and surging Treasury yields fueled inflation concerns, reinforced by the Federal Reserve's hawkish bias. Pre-market trading saw futures decline, with megacap growth and chip stocks facing early selling pressure.

items.headline: Amgen Rises on Strong Performance
items.summary: Amgen Inc. ($AMGN) rose 2.6% today, closing at $413.08. It was noted as a major gainer for the Dow Jones Industrial Average, driven by its biopharmaceutical performance.

items.headline: Wolfspeed Soars on Loan Commitment
items.summary: Wolfspeed ($WOLF) soared 14% to $35.89 in morning trading after receiving a $1.5 billion conditional loan commitment from the U.S. Department of Defense to fund domestic silicon carbide production.

items.headline: Applied Digital Up on Revenue Growth
items.summary: Applied Digital ($APLD) saw its shares increase by 4.03% to $24.77 during premarket trading, following a report of over 300% increase in first-quarter revenue, primarily from its high-performance computing business.

items.headline: PepsiCo Gains Despite Profit Outlook Cut
items.summary: PepsiCo ($PEP) shares rose 2.4% in volatile trading. The company beat Q3 earnings and revenue estimates but cut its full-year profit outlook due to pressure in North American snacks.

items.headline: Intel Drops Amid Chip Sector Weakness
items.summary: Intel ($INTC) stock fell 3% to $109.87 today. This drop was part of a broader sell-off in chip stocks, with added pressure from concerns over Elon Musk's Terafab project.

items.headline: Nvidia Slips with Chip Stocks
items.summary: Nvidia ($NVDA) shares were down 1% to $234.02 today. The decline was observed across the chip sector amid rising Treasury yields and higher oil prices.

items.headline: AMD Shares Decline in Chip Sell-Off
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices ($AMD) stock traded down 2% to $632.96 today, as the semiconductor sector faced pressure from rising Treasury yields and oil prices.

items.headline: Tesla Shares Retreat Slightly
items.summary: Tesla ($TSLA) shares were down 0.81% to $374.56 today. Megacap growth stocks broadly faced headwinds in the session.

items.headline: Amazon Sees Modest Decline
items.summary: Amazon ($AMZN) shares were broadly lower by around 1% today, as megacap growth stocks experienced selling pressure.

items.headline: Micron Technology Drops
items.summary: Micron Technology ($MU) dropped 2.1% today, as part of a broader decline among chip-related companies.

items.headline: Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes Expected This Year
items.summary: Most Federal Reserve officials anticipate another interest rate increase this year to combat persistent inflation, having already raised the key rate to approximately 3.9% at their September 15-16 meeting. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller indicated flexibility in the timing of these hikes, while emphasizing the stable labor market and elevated inflation. Traders generally expect rates to hold steady in October, but a December hike remains on the table.

items.headline: Key Economic Data Releases in Focus
items.summary: Today's economic calendar included the weekly Initial Jobless Claims, which were forecast at 200,000 against a previous reading of 197,000, and Continuing Jobless Claims, expected at 1.7 million compared to the prior 1.701 million. The Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow estimate remained unchanged at 3.7%, and updates on the Federal Reserve's balance sheet were released. The U.S. Census Bureau also published new data from its Business Trends and Outlook Survey.

items.headline: Health Care Leads, Industrials Lag in Sector Performance
items.summary: In today's trading, the Health Care, Consumer Discretionary, and Consumer Staples sectors ended in positive territory, with Health Care leading the gains. Conversely, the Industrials sector experienced a notable decline, alongside the Materials and Real Estate sectors, reflecting a defensive shift in the market. Chip-related companies also saw significant drops.

items.headline: PepsiCo Reports Q3 Earnings, Bank of South Carolina Sees Strong Growth
items.summary: PepsiCo ($PEP) announced its third-quarter earnings, beating analyst estimates for both EPS and revenue, though it revised its full-year profit forecast downwards due to challenges in North American snack sales. Meanwhile, Bank of South Carolina Corporation ($BKSC) reported a nearly 13% increase in its unaudited third-quarter earnings.

items.headline: Amazon Overhauls Device Lineup; Chip Industry Faces Headwinds
items.summary: Amazon ($AMZN) debuted a new series of pricier Alexa tablets, discontinuing its budget-friendly Fire lineup. In the chip industry, despite forecasts of record quarterly profit from Samsung Electronics, sentiment for chip-related companies remained low, contributing to a broader decline in the sector.
